_comment: AWARE 2.0 Phase 3 Modal app spec — read by src/trainer/index.js to submit DPO training jobs. The actual Modal Image / Function objects are built from this config at trainer boot time. NO SECRETS LIVE IN THIS FILE. Modal tokens are read from process.env.<redacted-credential-name> / <redacted-credential-name> at runtime.

modal_volume.name: aware-training-data
modal_volume._comment: Modal Volume for persistent storage: DPO datasets uploaded by the AWARE trainer, weight checkpoints produced by training/run.py, and training logs. Survives across job runs.

qwen35-9b-base-cache._comment: Modal Volume for the base-model model weights. First run downloads from HuggingFace CDN via hf-transfer (~$0.30, ~5 min). Subsequent runs cache-hit (instant, $0). Created by the v13 smoke test (commit 410af62).

qwen35-dpo-checkpoints._comment: Modal Volume for LoRA adapter checkpoints produced by `swift rlhf --rlhf_type dpo`. Persists across runs; the trainer service reads the latest adapter for atomic symlink swap on /root/aware-data/active. Created by the v13 smoke test.

gpu._comment: Single A100-80GB is what ADR-020 Decision 2 budget allows (~$150/run @ 60 GPU-hours). The base-model 4-bit QLoRA path (validated by v13 smoke test, commit 410af62) loads 9.65B params at 4-bit ≈ 5 GB VRAM, leaving ~75 GB of headroom for LoRA adapters (~40 MB), gradients, and the DPO forward+backward pass.

resources._comment: 8 CPU cores for data loading + AZR self-play verification (the Python executor spawns subprocesses, so cores matter for parallel verification). 64 GB RAM (was 32 GB) is bumped for the base-model multimodal architecture: the vision encoder + multimodal glue adds ~10-15 GB of working memory on top of the 4-bit text decoder's ~5 GB. 64 GB gives 30% headroom for a full DPO training step.

_comment_timeout: 5 hours hard cap. A full 10K-pair DPO run on base-model (4-bit QLoRA via training-framework 4.3.0, batch 1, grad-accum 2, ctx 512) takes ~3-4 hours on A100-80GB (extrapolated from v13 smoke at 5.5-5.91s/it × 5000 steps = 7-8 hours; ctx=512 + 10K pairs = ~5000 effective steps). 5h gives 25% slack; if a job hits the cap, the trainer marks the run as failed in Postgres and continues with the next batch.

dpo_defaults._comment_base_model: base-model (June 2025, multimodal `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` architecture, 9.65B params, hybrid linear/full attention). Locked in by the v13 smoke test (commit 410af62, 13 attempts, v13 passed in 229.32 sec). The previous trained-model path (R1) is retained as a fallback option (override per-run via trainer service env AWARE_BASE_MODEL).
dpo_defaults._comment: Hyperparameters tuned for base-model 4-bit QLoRA on a single A100-80GB via training-framework 4.3.0. The smaller max_seq_length (512 vs 4096) and batch (1 vs 4) are conservative — the v13 smoke ran at 5.5-5.91s/it which gives plenty of headroom for a 10K-pair run on A100-80GB. Bump max_seq_length back to 4096 once the real dataset is flowing (expect ~30s/it at that size). Override per-run via trainer service env (AWARE_DPO_BETA, AWARE_DPO_LR, etc.).

checkpoint._comment: After training, training/run.py writes the merged 16-bit model to /root/aware-data/checkpoints/<run-id>/ and the LoRA adapter to /root/aware-data/checkpoints/<run-id>/adapter/. The trainer service (Node) reads these back via modal.Volume.read_only and performs an atomic symlink swap on /root/aware-data/active → <run-id>. This is the 'Weight checkpoint → atomic symlink swap' deliverable from ADR-020.

self_play._comment: The AZR self-play loop runs INSIDE the Modal container between DPO training runs. It uses training/run.py's gen_azr_corpus() to produce synthetic tasks, then calls azr.executor to verify them, then emits preference pairs. The corpus_size_target is the total number of synthetic (chosen, rejected) pairs to accumulate; a run trains on whatever's available up to that target.

metrics._comment: Training loss, DPO margin, and AZR pass rate are logged to Modal's dashboard AND to the aware_training_runs table in Postgres. The trainer service writes the run summary back to Postgres when the job completes.

failure_policy._comment: If a training job OOMs, hits the timeout, or fails to load the base model, retry up to max_retries with backoff. After max_retries, the trainer service marks the run as failed and continues.
